summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:
- **ASFA (42 U.S.C. §§ 671–675)** — court ‘reasonable efforts’ findings; permanency timelines  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a circuit court order directing DCFS to remove and reassign a caseworker team that had failed its statutory reporting duty, holding the order neither exceeded the Juvenile Court Act nor violated separation of powers.
key_cases.relevance: Illustrates judicial direction to the agency mid-case as a trigger for renewed agency action.
key_cases.quote: The ultimate determination of which caseworkers to assign to the matter, therefore, remained within the discretion of DCFS.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the circuit court could not disregard a DCFS administrative abuse finding by conducting its own de novo review, reversed the change of custody as against the manifest weight of the evidence, and reinstated DCFS as guardian with power to consent to adoption.
key_cases.relevance: Illustrates a guardian ad litem motion in juvenile court triggering renewed agency and judicial scrutiny of a placement.
key_cases.quote: The court, without authority, rejected an administrative finding that the Wards abused Austin after conducting a de novo review of the matter.

search_keywords: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

state_agency.name: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

mandatory_reporters: Medical personnel — physicians, residents, interns, psychiatrists, surgeons, dentists, dental hygienists, chiropractic and podiatric physicians, physician assistants, emergency medical technicians, physical and occupational therapists, acupuncturists, registered/licensed practical/advanced practice nurses, genetic counselors, respiratory care practitioners, home health aides, certified nursing assistants — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(1)

Social services and mental health personnel — licensed counselors, social workers, psychologists, marriage and family therapists, field personnel of Healthcare and Family Services, Public Health, Human Services, Human Rights and DCFS, General Assistance supervisors/administrators, social services administrators, substance abuse treatment personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(2)
Crisis intervention personnel — crisis line or hotline personnel, domestic violence program personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(3)

Education personnel — school personnel (administrators, certified and non-certified employees), personnel of institutions of higher education, educational advocates, school board members (to the extent required by subsection (d)), truant officers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(4)
Recreation or athletic program or facility personnel; athletic trainers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(5)
Child care personnel — early intervention providers, nursery school and early care and education center directors and staff, foster parents, homemakers, child care workers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(6)

Law enforcement personnel — law enforcement officers, Department of Juvenile Justice and Department of Corrections field personnel, probation officers, animal control officers and Department of Agriculture field investigators — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(7)
Funeral home directors and employees; coroners; medical examiners — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(8)
Any member of the clergy — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(9)
Medical, nursing, social work and counseling personnel of any office or clinic that provides abortions, abortion referrals, or contraceptives — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(10)
reporting_details: Illinois is not a universal-reporting state: only the professionals listed in 325 ILCS 5/4(a) must report, any other person may report voluntarily under 325 ILCS 5/4(f), and every report goes to the single statewide DCFS hotline required by 325 ILCS 5/7.6 (1-800-25-ABUSE / 1-800-252-2873).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours; immediately, regardless of the time of day or night, if the child's immediate safety or well-being is endangered or the family may flee (325 ILCS 5/7.4(b)(2))
60 days to determine "indicated" or "unfounded"; extendable in additional periods of up to 30 days for good cause (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Report may be deemed "undetermined" where a complete investigation was not possible (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
